title: Small Business Ads: Promote Locally with Nextdoor | Nextdoor

facts.fact: Nextdoor's website states that 1 in 3 US households are on Nextdoor.
facts.quote:
1 in 3

#### US households are on Nextdoor

facts.fact: Nextdoor's website states that 76% of neighbors have been influenced by a recommendation on Nextdoor.
facts.quote:
76%

#### of neighbors have been influenced by a recommendation on Nextdoor

facts.fact: Nextdoor's website states that 88% of neighbors shop at local businesses.
Nextdoor states that Business Pages can be claimed for free.
Nextdoor states that Business Posts are free for small businesses to engage neighbors locally.
facts.quote: Engage neighbors locally with free Business Posts

facts.fact: Nextdoor describes its free Business Page as a way to create an online presence on the platform.
facts.quote: Create an online presence with a free Business Page

facts.fact: Nextdoor states that Business Posts are free and appear in the neighborhood newsfeed.
facts.quote: Engage nearby neighbors with free posts that show up in the most visible part of Nextdoor, the neighborhood newsfeed.

facts.fact: Local business owners, casual service providers, and home service providers are listed as business types eligible to participate on Nextdoor.
facts.quote: Local business owners, casual service providers, and home service providers can all participate on Nextdoor.

facts.fact: Casual service providers (such as dog walkers or babysitters) need official business documents to verify their Business Page before posting messages to the nearby neighborhood newsfeed.
facts.quote: If you offer casual goods or services (dog walking, babysitting) you will need official business documents to verify your Business Page in order to post messages to the nearby neighborhood newsfeed.

facts.fact: To claim a Nextdoor Business Page, the person must be a business owner, employee, or other authorized representative of the business.
facts.quote: You must be a business owner, employee, or other authorized representative of the business.

facts.fact: Nextdoor states that business information on its platform comes from third-party public data or from members who created a recommendation or comment for a business and could not find an existing page.
facts.quote: Business information on Nextdoor comes from 3rd party public data, or Nextdoor members who’ve created a recommendation or comment for your business

facts.fact: Nextdoor advises not to connect a personal Nextdoor account with a business account if the business login will be shared with authorized employees.
facts.quote: Do not connect your personal Nextdoor account with your business account if you plan on sharing your business login information with authorized employees.

facts.fact: Nextdoor states that if the business does not select its own neighborhood as part of a post's audience, the post cannot be seen from a member account.
facts.quote: if you do not select your own neighborhood, you won’t be able to see your post from your member account.

facts.fact: Nextdoor business posts have an audience set by adjusting a radius around the business, and businesses can also manually select or deselect specific neighborhoods.
facts.quote: Finally select your audience by increasing or decreasing the radius around your business. You can also manually select or deselect specific neighborhoods.

facts.fact: Nextdoor's footer on the page carries a copyright notice dated 2026.
